results.note: The migrated_postgres session fixture (tests/test_migration.py:46-52) skips the entire live-Postgres suite unless TEST_DATABASE_URL or TEST_POSTGRES_CONTAINER is set. The CI workflow (.github/workflows/uf-verify.yml) now provisions a postgres:16 service, sets TEST_DATABASE_URL, and installs psql — a real fix over the prior attempt — but no gate output supplied to this judging pass shows these 4 tests actually running (not skipping) and passing. The generic 'test' gate exits 0 whether skipped or run, and the only prior captured output for this exact test file ('31 passed, 4 skipped') shows them skipped locally. I cannot execute commands in this review and have no dedicated gate proving live execution, so I cannot confirm the constraints were actually exercised end-to-end through psql against a running Postgres.

Test correctly targets the criterion (asset='SOL', measured_on='BTC', status='OK' expected to fail on the asset_match constraint; a matching UNAVAILABLE row expected to succeed), driven via real psql against the migrated schema — a genuine integration-style test, not an isolated unit test. But it lives inside the same skip-gated fixture as C1, and no gate result given to me confirms it actually ran rather than skipped in this pass.

Parametrized test correctly covers both drift directions (OK with NULL value; UNAVAILABLE with non-NULL value) against the value_iff_ok check, with matching accept-cases. Same unconfirmed-execution gap as C1/C2 applies — gated behind the same skip-without-Postgres fixture, no dedicated gate output proving it ran.
Correctly targets reason_required (UNAVAILABLE without reason rejected, UNAVAILABLE with reason accepted). Same unconfirmed-execution gap as C1-C3.

check_migrations() (ingest/migrate.py:16-39) enforces the YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_lowercase_name.sql naming pattern, rejects duplicate/out-of-order names, and detects post-hoc edits by comparing each migration's sha256 against supabase/migrations/checksums.sha256, raising on mismatch. The shipped migration 20260908140000_create_datapoints.sql matches the pattern and its recorded checksum. The deterministic gate 'uv run python -m ingest.migrate --check' exits 0 against the real repo state, directly proving this criterion.

note: Same core gap as the prior rejected verdict for this story: the SQL constraints and their paired reject/accept tests are well-designed, and this attempt (commit c110cf0) adds a real fix — CI now provisions a postgres:16 service, sets TEST_DATABASE_URL, and installs psql — but no gate output given to this pass proves the 4 live-Postgres tests actually executed (vs. silently skipped, as the only captured local run shows). Since I have no shell access in this review and no dedicated C1-C4 gate was supplied, I cannot upgrade C1-C4 from the prior rejection on code inspection alone; that would be inferring correctness rather than citing proof of execution. C5 remains soundly met by a real deterministic, non-DB gate. No signs of faked work — the tests are assertive and target the right SQL constraint names.
